full_judgment:
2. The predecessor-in-interest of the appellants instituted other Suit No. 150 of 1986 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Satkania against the respondents for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and also for perpetual injunction in respect of 1.3875 acres of land out of 1.85 acres, that is, to the extent of 12 annas shares as described in the schedule to the plaint. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, was that the suit property is a tank and the banks surrounding to it which is popularly known as "Bureer Pukur". In Moghi Chitta Survey the scheduled property was recorded as Taraf Syed Mohammad Arshad Kishmat Malik Rahman. The said Taraf never possessed the same. Abdul Aziz and Abdul Fattah had been in possession of the same. During CS operation the suit land was recorded as Nayabad Mohal and the same was recorded in the names of Abdul Aziz and Abdul Fattah. They possessed the suit property for more than 90 years. They also paid rents to the Government. The said tank was silted up gradually. Abdul Aziz and others settled .the same to Mofzulur Rahman, Abdul Gafur, Abdul Bari and All Hossain, the predecessor-in-interest of the defendant Nos.33-62. Mofzulur and others having been in possession of the said tank re-excavated the same spending huge amount. Of them, Ali Hossain was literate person and he acted as "Karjakark" of all family members. In RS operation, the tank was recorded in the names of Abdul Razzak and others, where it was mentioned that they were in permissive possession. After enforcement of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiffs became the raiyats under the Government. At present, the plaintiffs have been possessing the said tank. The predecessor of the defendant No.32 filed an application for drawing proceeding under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and, accordingly, a proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure bearing Miscellaneous Case No.8 of 1949 was started in respect of the suit property. In that Miscellaneous case, the Magistrate found the claim of the heirs of Ali Hossain, Golam Sultan and others sustainable and, accordingly, put them in possession of the suit property. The predecessors of the plaintiffs had been possessing the suit tank by rearing fish and planting trees on the bank of the tank within the knowledge of the defendants. The principal defendants have had no title and possession in the suit tank. They disclosed that the suit tank was taluki property of Azmatullah and Muzibullah and the same was purchased by Ezzad Ali and others in auction and, thereafter, the predecessor-in-interest of the defendants took settlement of the suit tank from them. The principal defendants, who are rich men, have been making plan to enter into the suit tank forcibly. Thus, the plaintiffs constrained to file the suit. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 1-4, the predecessors of the present respondent Nos. 1-19, contested the suit by filing a joint written statement contending, inter-alia, that the suit was not maintainable and the same was barred by principle of res-judicata. Their positive case, in short, was that the suit property was recorded in Moghi Chita Survey as Plot No.699 under Taraf Syed Md Arshad Azmatullah and Mujibullah were the tenants under the said Taraf. For arrear rent, the suit property was put in auction. Ijjat Ali, Mosharrof Ali and Anwar Ali auction purchased the same and got possession thereof. Those auction purchasers settled the same to Ali Mahmud on 25th Falgun, 1257 BS who possessed the suit tank by rearing and preserving fish therein and planting trees on the banks. Ali Mahmud died leaving behind two sons namely Abdul Ali and Nazir Ali. On 22-7-1280 BS, Nazir Ali transferred his share to Abdul Ali by registered kabala deed. In the said kabala deed Ali Hossain was an attesting witness Abdul Ali became sole owner of the suit tank and constructed house beside the bank of the tank. The land-lords collected rent from Abdul Ali and others. Meanwhile, the suit tank was recorded in the names of Abdul Aziz and Abdul Fattah in the cadastral survey. Such record was wrong and baseless. The Government acquired no right or title in the suit land and it was never made khas land of the Government. The tank was never included in Nayabad Mahal. Abdul Aziz and Abdul Fattah never possessed the suit tank. Preparation of the RS Khatian following the CS record of right in the names of Abdul Aziz and others was equally wrong and never acted upon. The predecessors of the plaintiffs and proforma-defendant Nos.33-62 fabricated the so-called unregistered patta dated 10-5-1913. The predecessors of the plaintiffs claimed the suit land as their purchased land in Other Suit No. 17 of 1957 but failed to produce any deed and did not disclose about the existence of patta dated 10-5-1913. At the time of RS operation, Abdul Ali, predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-4, went to Rangoon for earning money and he entrusted his brother-in-law Ali Hossain to get the tank recorded in his name but Ali Hossain managed to get the same recorded in the names of Syed Abdul Aziz and others with the remarks therewith as permissive possession of Ali Hossain. After returning from Rangoon, Abdul Ali died leaving behind two sons, defendant No.1 and Jobbar Ali, and two daughters. The defendant No. 1 and his brother Jobbar Ali and sister Amena Khatun instituted Other Suit No. 17 of 1957 and obtained a decree for declaration of their title in respect of the suit tank. The defendant Nos. 1-14 and 15 of the said suit filed two different appeals being Nos.498 of 1958 and 27 of 1959 in the Court of District Judge which were dismissed on contest and, there-after, Second Appeal No.505 of 1963 was preferred in the High Court Division which was also dismissed. The plaintiffs never had any title or possession in the suit tank and, as such, the suit filed by the plaintiffs was liable to be dismissed. 

 10. It appears from the judgment of the High Court Division that initially the plaintiffs claimed title in the suit land on the basis of settlement but, at the time of hearing the Rule in the High Court Division, the learned Counsel for the plaintiff-appellants, giving go by to their claim of title on the basis of settlement, asserted their title in the suit land by way of adverse possession only stating that the plaintiffs' predecessors-in-interest and, thereafter the plaintiffs had been and have been possessing the suit land for more than 90 years. It appears from the schedule to the plaint that the plaintiffs prayed for decree firstly on the basis of the settlement and, thereafter, on adverse possession in respect of 1.383/4 acres of land out of 1.85 acres. Admittedly, the nature of the land is pond. It is case of the plaintiffs that the proforma-defendant Nos.33-62 are the owners of ¼th of the total land. It is not the case of the plaintiffs that there was any metes and bound partition amongst the co-sharers of the disputed land. Since plaintiffs' case is that the defendant Nos.33-62 are the co-sharers of the scheduled tank and banks of the same and that there was no metes and bound partition amongst the co-sharers, it is difficult to accept the submission of Mr AJ Mohammad Ali that the plaintiffs have been exclusively, uninterruptedly and peacefully possessing the suit tank. To establish the plea of adverse possession against a co-owners unambiguous evidence of complete ouster to their knowledge must be established. It is rebuttable presumption that the co-sharers in exclusive possession is holding possession on behalf of the other co-sharers. Possession of one co-owner is in law possession of all the co-sharers. Nothing sought of ouster or something equivalent to ouster will put an end to that possession. In order to establish adverse possession on the part of one of the co-sharer as against another it is not sufficient to show that one of them is in sole possession and enjoyment of the profit of the property. Ouster of the non-possessing co-sharers by co-sharing possession, who claimed his possession to be adverse should be made out. For this there must be evidence of open assertion of hostile title couple with exclusive possession and enjoyment by one co-sharer to the knowledge others. The burden of making out such ouster being on the person claimed into dispute the lawful title of a co-sharer by adverse possession. The concept of adverse possession contemplates a hostile possession i.e. a possession which is expressly or impliedly in denial of the title of the true owner. It is well-recognized proposition of law that mere possession, however, long does not necessarily mean that it is adverse to the true owner. The classical requirements of acquisition of title by adverse possession are that such possession in denial of the true owner's title must be peaceful, open and continuous.
